clue.text: Work together with company men in boring meeting

indicators.note: to bore is to drill through, so one piece sits inside the other like a drill in a hole

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers
taken as written
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Employees are told to collaborate with the firm's staff during a tedious meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring meeting' reads as a dull get-together, but 'boring' is the instruction to drill IN into DATE. OR for men is a military convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate is to organise people so they act in harmony and cooperate on a shared task.

clue.text: Drug supplier caught students leaving pub

indicators.note: whatever is leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out of the word

blocks.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
L is a learner, so two of them are students
a local is the pub nearest your home, in British usage

explanation.surface: A dealer is arrested as students walk out of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: LOCAL loses both its Ls to leave OCA. 'Drug supplier' sounds like a person, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca is the South American shrub whose leaves are the source of cocaine, so it literally supplies that narcotic.

clue.text: Hum, being inspired by notes regularly selected for instrument

indicators.note: picking at regular intervals means every other letter is kept
to be inspired is to be breathed in, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: a hum is a bad smell in British slang, and BO is body odour
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: Someone hums, inspired by a scattering of notes picked for an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hum' looks musical, but in British slang a hum is a bad smell, hence body odour.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument found in every orchestra.

clue.text: Without hope and the desire to be stimulated

indicators.note: something stimulated is stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone lacking hope and the wish to be roused into action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And the desire' looks like the continuation of a sentence, but it is exactly the twelve letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disheartened means having lost confidence or spirit, so feeling discouraged and deprived of optimism.

clue.text: Nothing picked up by informer’s circle

indicators.note: what is picked up is held by the picker, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: zero looks like the letter O
a nose is slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A grass's circle of contacts has heard nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'has': the informer has nothing picked up. NOSE as informer is old police slang, one who sniffs out information.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot, a ring that tightens when pulled.

clue.text: Medication upset maiden found in river

indicators.note: to be found inside something is to sit within it

blocks.note: to eat someone is to bother them, as in 'what's eating you?'
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A girl who was upset, and in need of medication, is found in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an anagram or reversal signal but is the verb EAT, as in something eating you. The Trent is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is medical care given to a patient, which includes drugs administered as a remedy.

clue.text: Video of motor racing starts in Le Mans

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: Formula 1, written F1 with the digit as the letter I
the opening letters of both words

explanation.surface: Footage of a motor race, the start at the Le Mans 24-hour race.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Mans hosts a famous sports car race, which steers you to the race itself; it only supplies two initials. The digit 1 in F1 stands as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A film and a video are both recorded moving pictures, so one word serves for the other.

clue.text: Freezing Italian sauces tipped over sweet powder

indicators.note: something tipped over is turned upside down, which in a down entry runs it backwards

blocks.note: icing is ice forming, as on an aircraft wing
ragù is an Italian meat sauce

explanation.surface: Frozen Italian sauces are knocked over onto a sweet powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freezing' looks like a description of the sauces, but it is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing sugar is finely ground sugar used for frosting cakes, a fine sweet dust.

clue.text: Charlatan’s horse underwritten by online fund

indicators.note: in a down entry, being written above something means coming before it

blocks.note: a mount is a horse for riding
E- is the prefix for electronic, as in e-commerce
a bank is a store or fund of money

explanation.surface: A con man's racehorse is financed by an internet investment fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underwritten' sounds financial, guaranteeing a risk, but here it means written underneath. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountebank was originally a quack who climbed a bench to sell fake remedies; now any swindling impostor.

clue.text: Spooner’s to control coven’s emblem of death

indicators.note: Spooner was a don famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: to boss is to control; it keeps its ending but takes the other word's opening sound
a coven is a gathering of witches, pictured as old crones; it keeps its ending but takes the other word's opening sound

explanation.surface: How to take charge of a witches' coven's symbol of death.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BOSS and CRONES to get CROSS and BONES.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbones, a pair of crossed thigh bones under a skull, mark poison or pirates and symbolise mortality.

clue.text: Place John in profession

indicators.note: to profess is to declare openly, so a profession here is something spoken

blocks.note: a john is American slang for a toilet, a loo in Britain

explanation.surface: Getting John a job in a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Profession' looks like a career, but here it is a statement made out loud. Loo is British for toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, surviving mainly in the phrase 'in lieu of', meaning instead of.

clue.text: Irresolute dim boozers primarily feel need to get drunk

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter counts
drunk means unsteady and confused, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Indecisive, slow-witted drinkers feel the urge to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim' looks like part of the definition but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble-minded can mean weak of will as well as of intellect, lacking the firmness to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Record three full scores and 90pc of another

definitions.text: three full scores and 90pc of another

blocks.note: first meaning: an old shellac gramophone disc played at that many rpm

blocks.clueFragment: three full scores and 90pc of another
blocks.note: second meaning: a sum, three twenties plus nine tenths of a fourth twenty

explanation.surface: Setting a record with three perfect scores and nearly a fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so three scores make sixty and 90 per cent of twenty is eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Before vinyl LPs, gramophone discs spun at 78 revolutions per minute, so they were called by that number.

clue.text: 6 photographer for Deadly Weapon

blocks.note: the number written in words
a photographer shoots pictures

explanation.surface: A cameraman for the next instalment of a film franchise called Deadly Weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' looks like a cross-reference to 6 across, FILM, which fits the movie picture; here it is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-shooter is a revolver holding six rounds, a gun capable of killing.

clue.text: Idealistic novel printed just so

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idealistic novel that was printed exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, but it is the signal to rearrange. 'Just so' is a slanted joke: printed sloping, the way emphasis is shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Italicised text is set in sloping type, used to emphasise a word such as 'so' in print.

clue.text: Act as advocate developing EC trade in energy without reference to America

indicators.note: to leave something without mention is to drop it entirely
something developing is changing shape, so the letters take a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy
A is a standard abbreviation for America, and it is removed

explanation.surface: Lobbying for European trade in energy while ignoring the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the European Community. Drop one A from the gathered letters, then rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to plead on someone else's behalf, which is exactly what an advocate does.

clue.text: Life sentence reduced by almost half after discrimination exposed

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of covering, so the outer letters come off
cutting nearly half away leaves a little more than half of the word

blocks.note: sexism is discrimination by gender
taken as written

explanation.surface: A life sentence is cut nearly in half after prejudice comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Life sentence' looks like one phrase, but 'Life' is the definition. Removing three of eight letters is the 'almost half'.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence is the state of being alive, so it serves as a synonym for life in general.

clue.text: Brief enticement to be enthralled by books?

definitions.text: Brief enticement to be enthralled by books?

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
someone enthralled is held captive, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: B is book, so two of them make books
a lure is an enticement

explanation.surface: A short come-on to get you gripped by reading.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while also building it: shortened LURE held by two Bs.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short promotional text on a book jacket, written to tempt a browser into buying and reading it.

clue.text: Going around Las Vegas, short of fuel and lubricant

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so those letters go
going around suggests spinning or circulating, so the letters move about

blocks.note: taken as written
gas is fuel, and American for petrol

explanation.surface: Driving around Las Vegas while running low on petrol and oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuel and lubricant' looks like one list of car fluids; 'and' splits them, leaving 'lubricant' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing ointment, a greasy substance smoothed on the skin, so loosely an oil or lubricant.

clue.text: At sea, mostly

blocks.note: first meaning: on the ocean, the main being a poetic word for the open sea
second meaning: for the most part, generally

explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea, mostly' reads as being confused much of the time; split it into two meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'on the high seas' literally and 'generally, on the whole' idiomatically.

clue.text: In performance, Richter was essentially tops here

definitions.text: In performance, Richter was essentially tops here

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter is kept
a performance is a rendering of a work, so the letters are played out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the central letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sviatoslav Richter, the great Soviet pianist, gave his finest concerts at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: in a performance a pianist like Richter would play from the orchestra pit, while the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra pit is the sunken area before a stage where musicians play during a performance.

clue.text: What one may pay to reach island?

blocks.note: a means one
the fee charged for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: How much does it cost to get to the island?
explanation.walkthrough: The question invites a price, but the answer is the phrase 'a toll' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or island surrounding a lagoon.

clue.text: Lampeter’s first cracking family baker

indicators.note: the first letter of a word is its opening one
to crack something open is to break into it, so one piece gets inside

blocks.note: kin are relatives
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A baker's family in Lampeter, a Welsh town, is doing a cracking trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baker' looks like a tradesperson, but it is anything that bakes, here pottery or bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln is an oven that fires clay or bricks at high heat, so it does the baking.

clue.text: Festival charge includes tea for the audience

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound
to include something is to hold it within

blocks.note: a fee is a charge
the drink is pronounced like the letter

explanation.surface: The admission charge at a festival covers a cup of tea for the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audience' suggests a crowd at the festival, but it signals sound: the drink becomes a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is an outdoor fundraising fair, typical of an English village summer, so a type of festival.

clue.text: Labour triumvirate’s beginning to oust leader in cover-up?

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter
ousting a leader removes whoever is at the front, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: the opening letter
a mask covers up the face

explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' wants to be the political party, but it is plain work.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, so labour as a noun for a job or chore.

clue.text: Early at home — G&T in order

indicators.note: taking things in order means one after another in sequence

blocks.note: someone at home is in
G is the abbreviation for good, as on a school report
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.walkthrough: G&T looks like gin and tonic, but each letter is expanded into the word it abbreviates.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive in good time is to arrive with time to spare, ahead of the deadline.

clue.text: Rough game ends in débâcle

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its two outermost letters

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
first and last letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough game' reads as one phrase, but 'Rough' is the definition and the game is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean roughly made or crude, as in a rude shelter of branches.

clue.text: Beauty ties up Yankee dude who’s desperate, initially craving sensuous entertainment

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
tying something up binds it round, so one piece wraps the others

blocks.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

the opening letter
